original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Can the climbs of the fields of Cao Yifan's final #4610 word be made coarser (fewer, larger-rank children) by freely reordering the scalar operations within their value dependencies, jointly re-choosing every field's frame chain and every contact's common frame, and letting the owned-centre reads move along the source chains, while the operation set, the native maps, the field endpoints and the centre delivery frame stay fixed?
scope_change_reason: #5226 prices the whole gap between #4610 and the +0.05% bar as fragmentation loss Lambda; its ship test asks which scalar-program changes can merge climbs. #4993 and #4610's own MILP moved frames at fixed chronology; #4610 lists a changed chronological order as open. This package frees the order and asks the question exactly for single-level merges, with an exhaustive feasibility check, instead of synthesizing a decoder.
bottleneck_link: Side result; no new kappa. The fragmentation of #4610 (23.86 per call; Lambda = 0 would allow 0.0081 in the kap family) cannot be reduced by any rescheduling: it is a property of the operation set and the centre interface.
stop_rule: Stop after the exhaustive single-level drop enumeration under the exact rules and the recorded annealing evidence for multi-step moves; do not synthesize a new operation set.
evidence: verify.py rebuilds the word, its dependency DAG and level graph, enumerates every admissible re-routing of the 2,526 droppable levels (518,315 re-routings) and certifies by an exact acyclicity check that none lowers the bill (the only 8 feasible ones move a centre read to the full frame, +0.983 each); a control that ignores the centre interface finds 51 improving drops; the kap-family ceilings quantify what Lambda would buy. search/ records 37 million simulated-annealing moves with multi-step insert/re-route/drop that found no improvement.

open_questions.question: Is there a skeleton-free fragmentation floor: does every scalar synthesis of the #4610 endpoint identity with one common frame per ADD need at least a stated number of intermediate levels per main field?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Lambda = 0 would allow kappa 0.0081 in the kap family and 0.0071 at the p16 controller; a floor would show how much of that is reachable by any word of this family.
open_questions.blocked_by: No argument that ties the number of contact levels to the native map; frame/endpoint relaxations alone force nothing (12 of 2,754 levels), the rigidity here comes from the joint chains and the centre interface.
open_questions.first_step: Formulate the chain-cover problem for the contact hypergraph with free frames and solve its LP relaxation over the 4,615 candidate frames.

open_questions.question: Can a different operation set (a new scalar program for the same endpoint identity, e.g. after the commuting-ADD compression of research/cao-trace-retiming-20261023) admit level drops?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This package fixes the operation set; compression removes operations and may remove contacts that pin levels.
open_questions.blocked_by: Needs the compressed word as a frozen input and the same enumeration on it.
open_questions.first_step: Run verify.py's drop enumeration on the compressed word of cao-trace-retiming-20261023 (same model).
